/cards/30/segments/0/text: After {{e_manuel|Manuel}} died, [[NPC1]] would not approach the building again. He walked for long hours, took detours, then drifted back to wander two streets away. The landlord could not arrange everything. He sent for the woman who had raised the brothers.
/cards/30/segments/1/text: [[NPC2]] came, gave clear and practical instructions, then went to the corner. He watched her with both longing and suspicion. As she drew near, he turned his body and averted his face.
/cards/30/segments/2/text: Will you help me a little? Come in and see your brother. Stay with me a while.
/cards/30/segments/4/text: She remembered the boys sitting at her knee while she told the story of the crucifixion. One had suddenly declared that, had they been there, they would have prevented it. Now this young man could not cross a familiar threshold. She did not reproach him. She changed the question and asked which brother he was.
/cards/30/segments/6/text: Using the name he gave, she continued asking him to come inside. She recalled his errands for her and the soup he had brought when she was ill, without listing her own kindnesses to him. When at last she spoke of her own losses and of God's ordering of things, the young man slowly walked away. Twenty paces later he stopped again.
/cards/30/segments/7/text: On the day of the funeral, candles burned even in daylight. Figures in black hoods sang a fearful hymn. He did not join the procession. He followed along parallel streets, reaching a crossing, glimpsing the line of people, then losing sight of it again.
/cards/31/segments/0/text: She asked which one I was. I said {{e_manuel|Manuel}}. People always confused us before, and we did not always correct them. So long as the other was there, whether we corrected the same mistake hardly seemed to matter.
/cards/31/segments/1/text: {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}} called that name and asked me inside. She did not say my answer was wrong. She only said she needed my help. I heard her mention the soup, the roads we used to take on errands. I remembered everything. Why had this short distance she wanted me to walk become so far?
/cards/31/segments/2/text: I do not want to return to the {{e_room|Brothers' Room}}, yet my walking always brings me near it. Around this street, then another, as though I am still on an unfinished errand. People pass me. None of them has to learn their old roads over again.
/cards/31/segments/3/text: She said that she had lost someone too. I wanted to listen, and feared that next she would tell me how it ought to pass. So I walked away, then stopped and looked back. Someone behind me called. I did not know which name to return under.
/cards/32/segments/0/text: For months, reports of the young man came from everywhere. Someone had seen him in a dry riverbed, someone among ancient ruins; a shepherd found him standing on a mountain, wet with dew. He took work driving carts or tending sheep, stayed a while, then left without a word. He travelled far, but always returned to Lima.
/cards/32/segments/1/text: A nun ran to tell [[NPC1]] that [[NPC2]] was outside again. She had imagined many ways to meet him: how could someone who had lost his brother be brought to live among people again? Now she suppressed her urgency and went to the door as calmly as she could.
/cards/32/segments/3/text: He stood trembling. She had seen the longing and distrust in those eyes before. She did not immediately ask for help or summon him inside. She merely repeated softly:
/cards/32/segments/5/text: She took a step forward. He suddenly turned and ran. Stumbling back to her desk, she knelt and angrily questioned God. She had prayed continually for wisdom; why had she received none? She was nothing but a scrubber of floors.
/cards/32/segments/6/text: She punished herself for these words, but the punishment did not remove the problem before her. During that time she thought of {{e_captain|Captain Alvarado}}. Three weeks later they spoke for ten minutes. The following day he went in search of the young man, said to be copying for the university in Cuzco. One failed attempt to hold him had finally become a request for another person's help.
/cards/33/segments/0/text: I have climbed these backstage stairs so often, carrying copied {{e_scripts|Spanish Plays}} up and coming down again. I used to think only of finishing the errand and leaving. Now at the door, with nothing in my hands, I cannot explain why I have come.
/cards/33/segments/1/text: {{e_camila|Camila}} sees me. I want badly to speak, but what should I say? That I am not the man who wrote her letters? Or that he can never come again? Once she drew us side by side and confidently declared one of us the younger. With only one face left, will she be more likely to mistake it?
/cards/33/segments/2/text: There is a mirror and there are things for the stage. I remember that midnight when she leaned close to {{e_manuel|Manuel}}'s ear. From the bed I thought there was no place left for me. Later the place became empty again. Nothing returned to what it had been.
/cards/33/segments/3/text: She waits. I look at her and still cannot find the sentence. The stairs are behind me. I go down them again. This time no one will ask why delivering a piece of work took so long.
/cards/34/segments/0/text: [[NPC1]] entered the dim kitchen without greeting the young man at once. [[NPC2]] moved his chair farther into shadow. They had unloaded ships together before; none of the three had liked idle talk. The sailor's arrival pleased him a little and made him want to hide. Only when the meal was finished did the older man approach.
/cards/34/segments/1/text: You have unloaded ships for me. I need strong men for my next voyage. Will you come? England, and Russia. Hard work, good pay, a long way from Peru.
/cards/34/segments/2/text: The young man stared at the table and did not answer for a long while. The captain repeated the question.
/cards/34/segments/4/text: Good. Naturally I would like your brother to come too.
/cards/34/segments/6/text: Does he not want to? Let me talk to him. Where is he?
/cards/34/segments/8/text: Both looked at the floor. When the captain asked his name, he gave his own this time. He did not borrow the other one.
/cards/34/segments/10/text: A few weeks ago. He hurt his knee. Only a few weeks.
/cards/34/segments/12/text: Twenty-two. I must go. I have something to do in town.
/cards/34/segments/13/text: Then come back this evening. Have supper with me and we will discuss the voyage. Come and have a little wine, will you?
/cards/34/segments/15/text: Neither found a sentence that could explain death. What remained at the table was simply a promise that could be kept: tonight, come back and sit here a while.
/cards/35/segments/0/text: Keep giving me work aboard, {{e_captain|Captain Alvarado}}. Anything. If the day is not enough, the night will do; I do not sleep well anyway. Do not leave me sitting there, waiting for the next bell.
/cards/35/segments/1/text: And do not tell the others about me. I know they may mean well. But when they fall silent and look at me, I do not know how to stand. Pretend you never knew me. Give me the most work. Do not make me feel I am the one being specially watched.
/cards/35/segments/2/text: I cannot copy at the desk anymore. The {{e_scripts|Spanish Plays}} lie before me, their words all neatly arranged, and still it seems another pen ought to be beside mine. Sometimes I would rather be too tired to think.
/cards/35/segments/3/text: You asked about a man I once rescued. I remember that, and why I suddenly changed the subject while speaking of it. We once had a dog—no, not that now. Do you know {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}}? There is something I want to do for her before we leave.
/cards/36/segments/0/text: Before leaving I want to give {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}} a {{e_gift|Gift}}. Could I have my wages in advance? I shall not need money away. I want to buy it now.
/cards/36/segments/1/text: Certainly. We will choose something in the morning.
/cards/36/segments/2/text: It would not be from me alone. Once she… she once…
/cards/36/segments/3/text: [[NPC1]] tried to speak his brother's name and could not. More quietly he mentioned that the abbess herself had told him of a terrible loss. He did not know whom she had lost, but had remembered her words.
/cards/36/segments/4/text: I want to give her something. A thing like that is hard for her to bear.
/cards/36/segments/5/text: He spoke for a long time. [[NPC2]] listened and promised to see to it the next day. When the young man fell forward in drunkenness, the captain went into the square outside the inn and looked at the mountains and clusters of stars. He too remembered a voice: do not be away too long; I shall be a big girl when you return.
/cards/36/segments/6/text: His daughter was dead. {{e_maria|María}} had once heard him speak of her and put the story into a letter to her own daughter. Sometimes, he said, he felt the child was merely travelling—perhaps in England—and that he might see her again after a little while. No voyage, however far, had entirely left that illusion behind.
/cards/36/segments/7/text: The captain went indoors, carried the young man to his room and sat watching him for a long time. Tomorrow's present still had no name. The person who had promised to arrange it was already here. The gift would belong to both brothers. For now, care had to begin with one living person.
/cards/37/segments/0/text: Morning has come in {{e_cuzco|Cuzco}}. Yesterday I agreed. Standing on the stairs today, I discover that agreeing did not finish the matter. {{e_captain|Captain Alvarado}} waits below. Suddenly I say that I cannot go, cannot leave Peru after all.
/cards/37/segments/1/text: He does not raise his voice. He asks about the present for {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}}. That was real; I do not want to take it back. She said she too had lost someone. I remember. Last night I tried to add another name to the gift and could not make my mouth say it.
/cards/37/segments/2/text: Usually {{e_manuel|Manuel}} decided. Another job, another place: we could always go together. This time wherever I go, there will be only one person's footsteps. If I stay, the familiar roads have not changed either.
/cards/37/segments/3/text: The captain says there will be work at sea. I need only fetch my things. I turn upstairs and walk that short distance very slowly. There is still someone outside waiting for me. I know he is there. I still do not know how to bring myself back to him.
/cards/38/segments/0/text: [[NPC1]] waited downstairs for a long time. He climbed part of the staircase and stopped to listen. At first there was no sound. Then a movement within told him that the young man was in danger.
/cards/38/segments/1/text: He had known unbearable moments himself. For an instant he could not tell whether intervening would help. The hesitation lasted only a moment. He rushed upstairs, pushed open the door and caught hold of [[NPC2]], stopping what was happening.
/cards/38/segments/2/text: Go away. Leave me alone. Do not come in now.
/cards/38/segments/3/text: The young man sank to the floor, repeating that he was alone. The captain stood beside him, his face grey, his old suffering awakened. Knowing stars, currents and headlands did not mean he could find words of comfort. Away from matters of navigation, he had always spoken awkwardly.
/cards/38/segments/4/text: We can only try. Try to go on. Time keeps passing. One day we shall be astonished that it has passed.
/cards/38/segments/5/text: He did not know whether his words had been heard, and did not offer them as a guarantee. The young man did not rise at once. Someone speaking did not suddenly restore the whole meaning of life. There was simply another person in the room who was willing to stay.
/cards/38/segments/6/text: The promised {{e_gift|Gift}}, the harbour and the next voyage were all waiting beyond the door. For now the captain did not urge him downstairs. He gave the morning to something smaller and nearer: remaining with him through this moment.
/cards/39/title: On the Bridge, by the River
/cards/39/segments/0/text: We set out. The roads are still the same roads: one stretch, then another. I have not suddenly become someone else. I have not left last night in a closed room. Someone is merely walking beside me, without requiring an explanation for every step I am willing to take.
/cards/39/segments/1/text: At the {{e_bridge|Bridge of San Luis Rey}}, {{e_captain|Captain Alvarado}} goes down to oversee the cargo crossing the river. It cannot go over this narrow footbridge; someone must attend to it by the water. I take the bridge. He goes about his work. We are supposed to meet again.
/cards/39/segments/2/text: The young man stepped onto the bridge. Below, the business of moving cargo continued; above, footsteps fell upon the thin boards. During this crossing the bridge broke. He fell with it.
/cards/39/segments/3/text: The captain remained below because of his work, not because he knew of any danger. There was no ceremony of farewell that day. Two people simply took two ordinarily unremarkable routes. Afterwards, when their voyage was mentioned, many sentences could go no farther than 'we were going to'.
